# The Hadwiger-Nelson Problem

The Hadwiger-Nelson problem asks for the minimum number of colors required to
color the plane such that no two points at unit distance from each other have
the same color.

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger%E2%80%93Nelson_problem)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«508»`.
-/

@[expose] public section

sources_consulted: Aubrey D. N. J. de Grey, The chromatic number of the plane is at least 5, arXiv:1804.02385; LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1804.02385, abstract and introduction.

review.notes: The reviewed file is a forwarding module with no local mathematical declarations. Its description and its pointer to Erdos508 faithfully match the cited Wikipedia problem. The imported formulation uses all points of the Euclidean plane, adjacency exactly at distance 1, and the minimum number of colors. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, sorry-free proofs verify equivalence with arbitrary functions from the plane to Fin n separating unit-distance pairs, and with the least permissible number n. Euclidean-distance, zero-color, empty-graph, singleton-graph, and infinite-chromatic-number checks passed. The imported lower-bound-three proof has no sorry dependency. Wikipedia still records the exact value as open, between 5 and 7, consistent with the imported statements and status tags. The supplementary erdosproblems.com/508 page returned a Cloudflare 403 despite a descriptive User-Agent; the specified Wikipedia source and de Grey's primary paper were accessible and sufficient to settle faithfulness.
